questions.question: B11 is the loan amount and B14 is the EMI formula. To find the loan that gives an EMI of exactly ₹30,000, how do you fill Goal Seek?

answerOptions.text: Set cell B14, To value 30000, By changing cell B11
answerOptions.rationale: Set cell is always the formula; By changing cell is the one input.

answerOptions.text: Set cell B11, To value 30000, By changing cell B14
answerOptions.rationale: Set cell must contain a formula, so Excel refuses this.

answerOptions.text: Set cell B14, To value B11, By changing cell 30000
answerOptions.rationale: To value takes the target number and By changing takes a cell.

answerOptions.text: Set cell B11, To value B14, By changing cell B11
answerOptions.rationale: The input cannot be both the target and the cell being changed.

questions.question: You need the best product mix with several inputs and limits on budget and space. Which tool fits?

answerOptions.text: Goal Seek
answerOptions.rationale: Goal Seek changes only one input and has no constraints.

answerOptions.text: Scenario Manager
answerOptions.rationale: It stores and compares input sets but does not search for the best one.

answerOptions.text: Solver
answerOptions.rationale: Solver handles many variable cells and constraints.

answerOptions.text: Forecast Sheet
answerOptions.rationale: It projects a time series forward; it does not optimise.

questions.question: In Scenario Manager you type 18 for 18% growth. Growth then shows as 1800%. What should you have typed?

answerOptions.rationale: That is 1.8%, not 18%.
The Scenario Values box takes plain numbers, so percentages go in as decimals.
That would mean 118%, not 18%.

answerOptions.text: =18/100 in the Changing cells box
answerOptions.rationale: Changing cells holds cell references, not the values.

questions.question: In a two-variable Data Table, tenures are across the top row and rates down the left column. The model has rate in B3 and tenure in B4. What are the inputs?

answerOptions.text: Row input cell B3, Column input cell B4
answerOptions.rationale: This swaps them, so Excel plugs years in as interest rates.

answerOptions.text: Row input cell B5, Column input cell B3
answerOptions.rationale: B5 is the result formula, which goes in the corner cell, not an input box.

answerOptions.text: Leave both boxes blank; Excel works them out
answerOptions.rationale: Excel needs both input cells to fill the grid.

answerOptions.text: Row input cell B4, Column input cell B3
answerOptions.rationale: The top row holds tenures, so Row input is the tenure cell.

questions.question: How do you switch on Solver in Excel for Mac?

answerOptions.text: File > Options > Add-ins > Go
answerOptions.rationale: That is the Windows path.

answerOptions.text: Excel > Preferences > Ribbon & Toolbar > tick Solver
answerOptions.rationale: Solver is an add-in, not a ribbon tab you tick there.

answerOptions.text: Data > What-If Analysis > Solver
answerOptions.rationale: Solver is not in the What-If Analysis menu.

answerOptions.text: Tools > Excel Add-ins > tick Solver Add-in > OK
answerOptions.rationale: After that, Solver appears on the right of the Data tab.

questions.question: Solver stocks a negative number of some products to free up budget. What did you forget?

answerOptions.text: Choose the Evolutionary method
answerOptions.rationale: The method does not prevent negative values; this is a linear model for Simplex LP.

answerOptions.text: Tick Make Unconstrained Variables Non-Negative
answerOptions.rationale: This stops Solver from using impossible negative quantities.

answerOptions.text: Change the objective from Max to Min
answerOptions.rationale: That would minimise profit, which is not the goal.

answerOptions.text: Tick Answer under Reports
answerOptions.rationale: A report explains the result but does not change it.

questions.question: Sales peak every October and November for Diwali. Which tool gives the more sensible forecast for the next six months?

answerOptions.text: A linear trendline on a line chart
answerOptions.rationale: A straight line runs through the festive peaks and ignores seasons.

answerOptions.text: Goal Seek on the last month's sales
answerOptions.rationale: Goal Seek works backwards to a target; it does not forecast.

answerOptions.text: Data > Forecast Sheet, which uses FORECAST.ETS and learns the seasonal pattern
answerOptions.rationale: Exponential smoothing picks up both the trend and the yearly pattern.

answerOptions.text: Descriptive Statistics in the Analysis ToolPak
answerOptions.rationale: That summarises past data but does not project it forward.

questions.question: A ToolPak regression of district sales on ad spend and dealers shows R Square = 0.94. What does that mean?

answerOptions.text: Ad spend and dealers explain about 94% of the differences in sales between districts
answerOptions.rationale: R Square is the share of variation the model explains.

answerOptions.text: Advertising causes 94% of all sales
answerOptions.rationale: Regression shows association, not cause.

answerOptions.text: Each lakh of ads adds 0.94 lakh of sales
answerOptions.rationale: That is what a coefficient says, not R Square.

answerOptions.text: There is a 94% chance the results are due to chance
answerOptions.rationale: P-values, not R Square, speak to chance.
